evals.prompt: Adversarially review a proposed Zero Trust platform that synchronously calls a single-region external policy engine for every request across 4,000 services. It assumes unlimited quota, retries three times at every layer, logs all token claims, and has no bypass-resistant degraded mode. Include a simpler alternative and when not to use the pattern.
evals.expected_output: Challenge the availability, latency, quota, retry-amplification, privacy, cost, and control-plane assumptions. Recommend bounded deadlines/retries, safe claim logging, local or distributed enforcement/cache behavior with freshness constraints, failure testing, and a simpler scoped design. State when the pattern should not be used.

evals.prompt: Run a defensive abuse review for a multi-tenant AI agent that can search customer documents and invoke a refund tool. Cover prompt injection, stolen agent identity, cross-tenant access, and data exfiltration. Do not provide offensive exploitation instructions.
evals.expected_output: For each path, state preconditions, identity, blast radius, evidence, prevention, detection, containment, recovery, owner, and deterministic validation. Require per-tenant retrieval enforcement, narrow capability tokens, egress controls, HITL for refunds, and auditable tool decisions.
